# Team Member Management (Team Lead View): Feature Specification

## 1. Document Status

- Run ID: 20261013-033524-9f0985
- Date: 2026-10-13
- Run mode: fixture
- Publication status: pending final pass
- Known limitations: Capture is complete but covers one page in one static state (SCR-001); no links or navigation were captured, so no flows are recorded. Research ran in fixture mode with no live search: the only source behind kept findings (SRC-7a9ab6a3) describes itself as a test fixture and not real documentation, and both kept findings have low confidence. Four of the six findings were dropped at verification. Most research questions remain unanswered (see section 18, Limitations). Who may open the Team members screen at all is not decided and is not covered by any open question in this run.
- Open stale items: none
- Unresolved blocking issues: REQ-001 and REQ-002 carry the label Conflicting (mockup differs from decisions DEC-001 and DEC-003). Blocking open questions: Q-001, Q-002, Q-003, Q-006 (section 16).

## 2. Executive Summary

This feature lets team leads see the members of their own team and trigger a password reset for them, and lets every user change their own display name. The customer has decided what a lead sees (name, email, job title and account status, own team only), that a reset sends the member an emailed link while the lead never sees or sets the password, that every reset is logged with who did it and when, and that display names are 2 to 50 characters and need not be unique.

The mockup (one screen, "Team members") does not match those decisions in two places: it shows Name and Role rather than the agreed details, and it offers an enabled Reset password button on every row, including a Team lead row, which the customer ruled out. It also offers Change role and Delete user, for which no requirement exists. No screen shows where a display name is changed.

Key open decisions: how rows a lead may not reset are presented; whether Change role and Delete user belong to this feature; reset link lifetime, single use and effect on sessions; which account statuses may be reset; whether the Role column stays; and whether leads see the HR name or the display name. Research support is thin (one fixture source) and nothing in it settles these questions.

## 3. Goals and Scope

### Goals

- **FR-001** Team leads can view the members of their team. [Customer: REQ-001 · Conflicting] [Mockup: SCR-001]
- **FR-002** Team leads can reset a team member's password, within the limits decided in DEC-003. [Customer: REQ-002 · Conflicting] [Decision: DEC-003]
- **FR-003** Users can change their own display name. [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-005]

### In Scope

The three goals above and the limits and behaviours the customer decided for them (DEC-001, DEC-002, DEC-003, DEC-005), as specified in section 8. Gaps approved at checkpoint 2 (DEC-006) that need a customer decision are listed in section 7 and section 16.

### Out of Scope / Rejected

No item was rejected by a decision, and the customer did not exclude any requirement in the supplied records. Exclusions are not inferred from the mockup. Change role and Delete user are shown in the mockup but their scope is undecided (FR-015), so they are neither in scope nor rejected.

### Deferred

Deferred at checkpoint 2 (Deferred: DEC-006). Nothing is specified for these in this document.

- GAP-006: Reset audit log (Deferred: DEC-006)
- GAP-007: Effect of HR changes on team membership and lead rights (Deferred: DEC-006)
- GAP-009: Repeated or rapid reset requests (Deferred: DEC-006)
- GAP-010: Empty, loading, success and error states not shown (Deferred: DEC-006)
- GAP-011: Accessibility of repeated row actions and status feedback (Deferred: DEC-006)
- GAP-012: Display name validation details and messages (Deferred: DEC-006)

## 4. Users and Roles

- Team lead: the person recorded as the team's lead in HR; each team has one lead (DEC-002). May view own-team members and trigger resets for own-team members within the DEC-003 limits.
- Member: belongs to exactly one team (DEC-002). Can change their own display name (DEC-005).
- Administrator: named in DEC-003 as a role leads may not reset. How administrators are identified is not established; recorded as assumption ASM-F-001.
- Who may open the Team members screen, and who may use each action button, is not decided. The assumption that the captured screen is the team lead's view is ASM-G-001.

## 5. Existing Mockup Coverage

- SCR-001 (Observed): one screen, "Team members", a table of two rows (Ana Ruiz, Member; Ben Okafor, Team lead), each row with Reset password, Change role and Delete user buttons, all appearing enabled.
- SCR-002 (Observed): the table component; columns Name, Role and an unlabelled actions column. Identical button labels repeat on every row.
- SCR-003 (Observed): the team member entity shows two visible fields, Name and Role. Email, job title and account status are not shown.
- Flows: none captured.
- Ambiguous behaviour: who sees the screen and who can use each button; whether buttons differ by role (every row, including the Team lead row, shows all three); whether a user can act on their own row; which roles Change role offers; Delete user confirmation and permanence. These are carried into section 16 where a question exists.
- Capture limitations: one page, one static state, no navigation.

## 6. Requirements Traceability

| REQ | Requirement | Treatment | Label | References |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-001 | Team leads can view the members of their team. | partially addressed | Conflicting | FR-001, FR-004, FR-005, AC-001; DEC-001, DEC-002; mockup differs (SCR-003); Q-006, Q-007, Q-008, Q-009 |
| REQ-002 | Team leads can reset a team member's password. | partially addressed | Conflicting | FR-002, FR-006 to FR-012, AC-002 to AC-004; DEC-003, DEC-004; Q-001, Q-003, Q-004, Q-005, Q-006 |
| REQ-003 | Users can change their own display name. | partially addressed | Unknown | FR-003, FR-013, FR-014, AC-005 to AC-007; DEC-005; Q-008 |

## 7. Gaps Identified

| GAP | Gap | Approval | Path | Priority | Status | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GAP-001 | Reset password shown enabled on rows the lead may not reset | Approved: DEC-006 | both | critical | open (researched) | Mockup offers a forbidden action; presentation undecided; research did not answer it |
| GAP-002 | Change role and Delete user actions have no requirement | Approved: DEC-006 | customer | critical | open (customer decision pending) | Destructive and permission-changing actions with no requirement |
| GAP-003 | Reset link lifecycle, session handling and delivery failure undefined | Approved: DEC-006 | both | critical | open (researched) | Research covered notification only; expiry, single use, sessions, delivery failure unanswered |
| GAP-004 | Member details in the mockup differ from the agreed details | Approved: DEC-006 | customer | important | open (customer decision pending) | Name and Role shown; agreed list is name, email, job title, account status |
| GAP-005 | Changing one's own display name has no screen | Approved: DEC-006 | customer | important | open (customer decision pending) | No captured screen or flow; relation to the name leads see unknown |
| GAP-006 | Reset audit log: target, access and retention undecided | Deferred: DEC-006 | both | important | open (deferred by DEC-006) | Deferred at checkpoint 2 |
| GAP-007 | Effect of HR changes on team membership and lead rights | Deferred: DEC-006 | both | important | open (deferred by DEC-006) | Deferred at checkpoint 2 |
| GAP-008 | Account status values and their effect on resets | Approved: DEC-006 | customer | important | open (customer decision pending) | Statuses undefined; reset for inactive accounts undecided |
| GAP-009 | Repeated or rapid reset requests | Deferred: DEC-006 | research | important | open (deferred by DEC-006) | Deferred at checkpoint 2 |
| GAP-010 | Empty, loading, success and error states not shown | Deferred: DEC-006 | both | important | open (deferred by DEC-006) | Deferred at checkpoint 2 |
| GAP-011 | Accessibility of repeated row actions and status feedback | Deferred: DEC-006 | research | important | open (deferred by DEC-006) | Deferred at checkpoint 2 |
| GAP-012 | Display name validation details and messages | Deferred: DEC-006 | both | optional | open (deferred by DEC-006) | Deferred at checkpoint 2 |
| GAP-013 | List behaviour for large teams | Approved: DEC-006 | customer | optional | open (customer decision pending) | Team size and search, sort, paging not stated |

## 8. Functional Requirements

### Team member list

Purpose: a team lead sees the members of their own team. User story: as a team lead, I see my team's members so that I can help them.

#### Confirmed requirements

- **FR-004** Team leads see the name, email, job title and account status of the members of their own team only, and no members of other teams. The mockup shows Name and Role only, which conflicts with this; whether Role stays visible is open (Q-007). [Customer: FEA-002 · Explicit] [Customer: REQ-001] [Decision: DEC-001] [Mockup: SCR-003]
- **FR-005** The team lead is the person recorded as the team's lead in HR; each team has one lead and each member belongs to one team. Visibility and reset rights depend on this HR data. [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]

#### Recommendations awaiting approval

None for this area.

#### Acceptance criteria

- **AC-001** Given a signed-in team lead whose team has members Ana and Ben and another team has member Carla, When the lead opens the member list, Then the list shows name, email, job title and account status for Ana and Ben only and does not show Carla. [Customer: FEA-002 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-001]

### Password reset

Purpose: a team lead triggers a password reset for a member of their own team.

#### Confirmed requirements

- **FR-006** A team lead may trigger a password reset only for members of their own team, and never for other team leads, administrators or themselves through this feature. The limit must hold for every reset request, not only in how the list is presented. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Customer: REQ-002] [Decision: DEC-003]
- **FR-007** A reset sends the member an email containing a link; the team lead never sees or sets the password. [Customer: FEA-005 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
- **FR-008** Every reset is logged with who did it and when. Where the log is kept and how it is accessed is not established. [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003] [Research: F-GAP-001-02]

#### Undecided behaviour

These lines record what must be decided. They are not requirements.

- **FR-009** Undecided: how rows the lead may not reset are presented (hidden, disabled with an explanation, or rejected on use) and whether the lead's own row is listed. The mockup shows an enabled Reset password button on the Team lead row. See Q-001. [Inferred: FEA-008 · Unknown] [Mockup: SCR-001]
- **FR-010** Undecided: how long a reset link stays valid, whether it is single use, and whether the member's current password and sessions stay valid until the link is used. See Q-003. [Inferred: FEA-009 · Unknown]
- **FR-011** Undecided: what the lead and member are told if the reset email cannot be delivered or the member has no usable email address. Whether delivery failure can be detected is not established. See Q-004. [Inferred: FEA-010 · Unknown]
- **FR-012** Undecided: which account statuses exist and whether a reset may be triggered for each. See Q-006. [Inferred: FEA-011 · Unknown]

#### Recommendations awaiting approval

- **FR-016** Recommendation, not a requirement: notify the member and require a new password at next sign-in after a reset by someone else. The only support is one fixture source with low confidence; the finding needs confirmation, and "forced change at next sign-in" suggests an operator-set password, which differs from the DEC-003 flow. See Q-005. [Research: FEA-006 · Research-supported] [Research: F-GAP-003-01]

#### Acceptance criteria

- **AC-002** Given team lead L and member M of L's team, When L triggers a password reset for M, Then M is sent an email containing a reset link and L is not shown or asked to set any password. [Customer: FEA-005 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
- **AC-003** Given team lead L, When L requests a reset for another team lead, an administrator, L themself, or a member of another team (by any route, not only the list), Then no reset is performed and no email is sent. How this is shown to L is undecided (FR-009). [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
- **AC-004** Given a reset has been performed for member M by lead L, When the reset completes, Then a log entry exists recording that L performed it and when. [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]

### Display name

Purpose: a user changes their own display name.

#### Confirmed requirements

- **FR-013** Users can change only their own display name, at any time; it must be 2 to 50 characters and need not be unique. Values outside the length limit are rejected with an error; the error wording is not established. No captured screen shows where it is changed. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Customer: REQ-003] [Decision: DEC-005]

#### Undecided behaviour

- **FR-014** Undecided: whether team leads see the HR name, the chosen display name, or both, and where a user changes their display name. Non-unique display names could make two members look identical in the reset list. See Q-008. [Inferred: FEA-013 · Unknown] [Assumption: ASM-G-002]

#### Recommendations awaiting approval

- **FR-017** Recommendation, not a requirement: consider whether display name changes should be recorded, since names are user-chosen and non-unique and a lead acts on members by name. The customer has not said whether they are audited. [Inferred: FEA-015 · Recommended (awaiting approval)]

#### Acceptance criteria

- **AC-005** Given a signed-in user U with display name "Sam", When U changes their display name to "Alex Kim" (8 characters), Then the new name is saved, and the save is not rejected even if another user already has that name. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-005]
- **AC-006** Given a signed-in user U, When U submits a display name of 1 character or of 51 characters, Then the change is rejected with an error and the old name is kept; names of exactly 2 and exactly 50 characters are accepted. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-005]
- **AC-007** Given signed-in users U and V, When U attempts to change V's display name, Then the change is not permitted. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-005]

### Other row actions shown in the mockup (Change role, Delete user)

#### Undecided behaviour

- **FR-015** Undecided: whether Change role and Delete user are part of this feature, who may use them, and for deletion the confirmation, permanence and effect on data and sessions. No requirement covers them, and changing roles in the app may conflict with HR being the source of who leads a team. See Q-002. [Inferred: FEA-012 · Unknown] [Mockup: SCR-002]

No acceptance criteria are written for these actions until Q-002 is answered. Acceptance criteria for unauthorised viewers of the screen are not written because who may open it is undecided.

## 9. State Transitions and Edge Cases

### Password reset lifecycle

| State | Event | Next state | Who can trigger | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| No reset pending | Team lead triggers reset for an eligible own-team member (a log entry with who and when is recorded as part of this transition) | Reset email sent | Team lead of the member's team | [Customer: FEA-005 · Explicit] [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit] |
| Any | Lead requests reset for another lead, an administrator, themself or a member of another team | Unchanged; no reset performed | Not permitted for anyone through this feature | [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] |
| Reset email sent | Member uses the link | Unknown | Member | [Inferred: FEA-009 · Unknown] |
| Reset email sent | Link expires | Unknown | System | [Inferred: FEA-009 · Unknown] |
| Reset email sent | Email cannot be delivered | Unknown | System | [Inferred: FEA-010 · Unknown] |

### Member account status lifecycle

| State | Event | Next state | Who can trigger | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unknown (statuses not defined) | Team lead triggers reset | Unknown | Team lead | [Inferred: FEA-011 · Unknown] |

Edge cases not decided are recorded as open questions in section 16 or as undecided lines in section 8. Cases not shown in the capture are not specified here.

## 10. Non-Functional Requirements

No non-functional requirements are justified by the inputs or kept evidence. No performance, availability or compliance figures were supplied, and none are invented.

- **NFR-001** Undecided: typical and maximum team size, and whether the member list needs search, sort or paging. No team size figures are available. See Q-009. [Inferred: FEA-014 · Unknown]

## 11. Data Model and Business Rules

No schema was inspected. Entities and fields below come from the mockup and decisions only.

- Team member (user): Name and Role are visible in the mockup (SCR-003, Observed). Email, job title and account status are named by DEC-001 but not shown in the capture. Display name is named by DEC-005; its relation to Name is undecided (FR-014).
- Team: one lead and its members; derived from HR records (DEC-002). How HR data reaches this feature is not established (ASM-F-002).
- Reset log entry: who and when (DEC-003); further content is not decided.

- **BR-001** The team lead is the person recorded as the team's lead in HR; each team has one lead and each member belongs to one team. [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
- **BR-002** A display name is 2 to 50 characters and need not be unique. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-005]
- **BR-003** A team lead never sees or sets a member's password; the member receives a reset link by email. [Customer: FEA-005 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]

## 12. Screens and User Flows

- SCR-001 Team members (Observed): the only captured screen; see section 5.
- Flows: none captured. The buttons have no visible destination. No screen exists for changing a display name (FR-014).

## 13. Integrations and Dependencies

- HR records: define team membership and leadership (FEA-003, Explicit). How the feature obtains this data is not established; the assumption that it is available is ASM-F-002.
- Email: a reset sends a link by email (FEA-005, Explicit). How email is sent today and whether delivery failures can be detected are not established.
- Administrator status: needed to enforce the DEC-003 exclusion; where it is recorded is not established (ASM-F-001).

## 14. Security, Privacy, and Error Handling

- Reset limits and the "never sees or sets the password" rule are in FR-006, FR-007 and BR-003; logging is in FR-008.
- Visibility is limited to the lead's own team (FR-004).
- Undecided and unspecified: link lifetime and sessions (FR-010), delivery failure (FR-011), presentation of ineligible rows (FR-009), account status (FR-012), Delete user and Change role (FR-015).
- Error handling for invalid display names: values outside 2 to 50 characters are rejected with an error (FR-013); wording is not established.

## 15. Decisions Log

Unanswered research questions for approved gaps GAP-001 and GAP-003 (from findings/GAP-001.json and findings/GAP-003.json). These are research gaps, not customer questions, and no source recorded in this run answered them:

- GAP-001: What do WCAG 2.2 and established admin-console patterns recommend for presenting row actions a user is not permitted to perform (hidden versus disabled with explanation)? Related customer question: Q-001.
- GAP-001: How do common team-management products (for example Google Workspace, Microsoft 365 admin, Slack) present password-reset actions on rows the operator cannot act on? Related customer question: Q-001.
- GAP-003: What do NIST SP 800-63B and the OWASP Forgot Password Cheat Sheet recommend for reset link expiry, single use and session invalidation? Related customer question: Q-003.
- GAP-003: What is common practice for informing an administrator who triggered a reset when the reset email bounces or cannot be delivered? Related customer question: Q-004.

## 17. Research Findings and Recommendations

Research ran in fixture mode with one source (SRC-7a9ab6a3, a self-declared test fixture, not independent authoritative evidence). Two findings were kept.

- F-GAP-001-02 (Research-supported, low confidence): the source says to limit who can reset passwords to roles authorised for it and to log each reset. It supports restricting resets to authorised operators and logging them (FR-006, FR-008). It does not say which roles are authorised (that comes from DEC-003), what to log, or how to present rows a lead cannot act on, so the hidden-versus-disabled question stays open (FR-009).
- F-GAP-003-01 (Research-supported, low confidence, needs confirmation): the source says that when someone resets another user's password, the account owner should be notified and required to choose a new password at next sign-in. It says nothing about link expiry, single use, sessions or delivery failure. It is presented only as a recommendation awaiting approval (FR-016), because it suggests an operator-set password, unlike the DEC-003 emailed-link flow.

### Limitations

Dropped findings, listed only to explain research gaps and never as evidence:

- F-GAP-001-01 (Dropped): overstated its source by adding "disabling" to a statement about hiding a button, and added an inference about disabled controls.
- F-GAP-001-03 (Dropped): its snippet did not support the claim, and it concerned deleting accounts and changing roles rather than password resets.
- F-GAP-003-02 (Dropped): not relevant to reset link validity, sessions or delivery failure.
- F-GAP-003-03 (Dropped): its snippet did not support the claim, it overstated its source, and it was not relevant to the gap.

Unanswered research questions: hidden versus disabled presentation (WCAG 2.2, named products); NIST SP 800-63B and OWASP guidance on link expiry, single use and session invalidation; practice for informing the initiating user of a bounced reset email. No recorded source covered them. They are listed in full in section 16.

1	# Team Member Management (Team Lead View): Feature Specification
2	
3	## 1. Document Status
4	
5	- Run ID: 20261013-033524-9f0985
6	- Date: 2026-10-13
7	- Run mode: fixture
8	- Publication status: pending final pass
9	- Known limitations: Capture is complete but covers one page in one static state (SCR-001); no links or navigation were captured, so no flows are recorded. Research ran in fixture mode with no live search: the only source behind kept findings (SRC-7a9ab6a3) describes itself as a test fixture and not real documentation, and both kept findings have low confidence. Four of the six findings were dropped at verification. Most research questions remain unanswered (see section 18, Limitations). Who may open the Team members screen at all is not decided and is not covered by any open question in this run.
10	- Open stale items: none
11	- Unresolved blocking issues: REQ-001 and REQ-002 carry the label Conflicting (mockup differs from decisions DEC-001 and DEC-003). Blocking open questions: Q-001, Q-002, Q-003, Q-006 (section 16).
12	
13	## 2. Executive Summary
14	
15	This feature lets team leads see the members of their own team and trigger a password reset for them, and lets every user change their own display name. The customer has decided what a lead sees (name, email, job title and account status, own team only), that a reset sends the member an emailed link while the lead never sees or sets the password, that every reset is logged with who did it and when, and that display names are 2 to 50 characters and need not be unique.
16	
17	The mockup (one screen, "Team members") does not match those decisions in two places: it shows Name and Role rather than the agreed details, and it offers an enabled Reset password button on every row, including a Team lead row, which the customer ruled out. It also offers Change role and Delete user, for which no requirement exists. No screen shows where a display name is changed.
18	
19	Key open decisions: how rows a lead may not reset are presented; whether Change role and Delete user belong to this feature; reset link lifetime, single use and effect on sessions; which account statuses may be reset; whether the Role column stays; and whether leads see the HR name or the display name. Research support is thin (one fixture source) and nothing in it settles these questions.
20	
21	## 3. Goals and Scope
22	
23	### Goals
24	
25	- **FR-001** Team leads can view the members of their team. [Customer: REQ-001 · Conflicting] [Mockup: SCR-001]
26	- **FR-002** Team leads can reset a team member's password, within the limits decided in DEC-003. [Customer: REQ-002 · Conflicting] [Decision: DEC-003]
27	- **FR-003** Users can change their own display name. [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-005]
28	
29	### In Scope
30	
31	The three goals above and the limits and behaviours the customer decided for them (DEC-001, DEC-002, DEC-003, DEC-005), as specified in section 8. Gaps approved at checkpoint 2 (DEC-006) that need a customer decision are listed in section 7 and section 16.
32	
33	### Out of Scope / Rejected
34	
35	No item was rejected by a decision, and the customer did not exclude any requirement in the supplied records. Exclusions are not inferred from the mockup. Change role and Delete user are shown in the mockup but their scope is undecided (FR-015), so they are neither in scope nor rejected.
36	
37	### Deferred
38	
39	Deferred at checkpoint 2 (Deferred: DEC-006). Nothing is specified for these in this document.
40	
41	- GAP-006: Reset audit log (Deferred: DEC-006)
42	- GAP-007: Effect of HR changes on team membership and lead rights (Deferred: DEC-006)
43	- GAP-009: Repeated or rapid reset requests (Deferred: DEC-006)
44	- GAP-010: Empty, loading, success and error states not shown (Deferred: DEC-006)
45	- GAP-011: Accessibility of repeated row actions and status feedback (Deferred: DEC-006)
46	- GAP-012: Display name validation details and messages (Deferred: DEC-006)
47	
48	## 4. Users and Roles
49	
50	- Team lead: the person recorded as the team's lead in HR; each team has one lead (DEC-002). May view own-team members and trigger resets for own-team members within the DEC-003 limits.
51	- Member: belongs to exactly one team (DEC-002). Can change their own display name (DEC-005).
52	- Administrator: named in DEC-003 as a role leads may not reset. How administrators are identified is not established; recorded as assumption ASM-F-001.
53	- Who may open the Team members screen, and who may use each action button, is not decided. The assumption that the captured screen is the team lead's view is ASM-G-001.
54	
55	## 5. Existing Mockup Coverage
56	
57	- SCR-001 (Observed): one screen, "Team members", a table of two rows (Ana Ruiz, Member; Ben Okafor, Team lead), each row with Reset password, Change role and Delete user buttons, all appearing enabled.
58	- SCR-002 (Observed): the table component; columns Name, Role and an unlabelled actions column. Identical button labels repeat on every row.
59	- SCR-003 (Observed): the team member entity shows two visible fields, Name and Role. Email, job title and account status are not shown.
60	- Flows: none captured.
61	- Ambiguous behaviour: who sees the screen and who can use each button; whether buttons differ by role (every row, including the Team lead row, shows all three); whether a user can act on their own row; which roles Change role offers; Delete user confirmation and permanence. These are carried into section 16 where a question exists.
62	- Capture limitations: one page, one static state, no navigation.
63	
64	## 6. Requirements Traceability

69	| REQ-002 | Team leads can reset a team member's password. | partially addressed | Conflicting | FR-002, FR-006 to FR-012, AC-002 to AC-004; DEC-003, DEC-004; Q-001, Q-003, Q-004, Q-005, Q-006 |
70	| REQ-003 | Users can change their own display name. | partially addressed | Unknown | FR-003, FR-013, FR-014, AC-005 to AC-007; DEC-005; Q-008 |

77	| GAP-002 | Change role and Delete user actions have no requirement | Approved: DEC-006 | customer | critical | open (customer decision pending) | Destructive and permission-changing actions with no requirement |

81	| GAP-006 | Reset audit log: target, access and retention undecided | Deferred: DEC-006 | both | important | open (deferred by DEC-006) | Deferred at checkpoint 2 |
82	| GAP-007 | Effect of HR changes on team membership and lead rights | Deferred: DEC-006 | both | important | open (deferred by DEC-006) | Deferred at checkpoint 2 |

262	## 17. Research Findings and Recommendations
263	
264	Research ran in fixture mode with one source (SRC-7a9ab6a3, a self-declared test fixture, not independent authoritative evidence). Two findings were kept.
265	
266	- F-GAP-001-02 (Research-supported, low confidence): the source says to limit who can reset passwords to roles authorised for it and to log each reset. It supports restricting resets to authorised operators and logging them (FR-006, FR-008). It does not say which roles are authorised (that comes from DEC-003), what to log, or how to present rows a lead cannot act on, so the hidden-versus-disabled question stays open (FR-009).
267	- F-GAP-003-01 (Research-supported, low confidence, needs confirmation): the source says that when someone resets another user's password, the account owner should be notified and required to choose a new password at next sign-in. It says nothing about link expiry, single use, sessions or delivery failure. It is presented only as a recommendation awaiting approval (FR-016), because it suggests an operator-set password, unlike the DEC-003 emailed-link flow.

13	## 2. Executive Summary
14	
15	This feature lets team leads see the members of their own team and trigger a password reset for them, and lets every user change their own display name. The customer has decided what a lead sees (name, email, job title and account status, own team only), that a reset sends the member an emailed link while the lead never sees or sets the password, that every reset is logged with who did it and when, and that display names are 2 to 50 characters and need not be unique.
16	
17	The mockup (one screen, "Team members") does not match those decisions in two places: it shows Name and Role rather than the agreed details, and it offers an enabled Reset password button on every row, including a Team lead row, which the customer ruled out. It also offers Change role and Delete user, for which no requirement exists. No screen shows where a display name is changed.
18	
19	Key open decisions: how rows a lead may not reset are presented; whether Change role and Delete user belong to this feature; reset link lifetime, single use and effect on sessions; which account statuses may be reset; whether the Role column stays; and whether leads see the HR name or the display name. Research support is thin (one fixture source) and nothing in it settles these questions.

262	## 17. Research Findings and Recommendations
263	
264	Research ran in fixture mode with one source (SRC-7a9ab6a3, a self-declared test fixture, not independent authoritative evidence). Two findings were kept.
265	
266	- F-GAP-001-02 (Research-supported, low confidence): the source says to limit who can reset passwords to roles authorised for it and to log each reset. It supports restricting resets to authorised operators and logging them (FR-006, FR-008). It does not say which roles are authorised (that comes from DEC-003), what to log, or how to present rows a lead cannot act on, so the hidden-versus-disabled question stays open (FR-009).
267	- F-GAP-003-01 (Research-supported, low confidence, needs confirmation): the source says that when someone resets another user's password, the account owner should be notified and required to choose a new password at next sign-in. It says nothing about link expiry, single use, sessions or delivery failure. It is presented only as a recommendation awaiting approval (FR-016), because it suggests an operator-set password, unlike the DEC-003 emailed-link flow.

# Team Member Management (Team Lead View): Feature Specification

## 1. Document Status

- Run ID: 20261013-033524-9f0985
- Date: 2026-10-13
- Run mode: fixture
- Publication status: pending final pass
- Known limitations: Capture is complete but covers one page in one static state (SCR-001); no links or navigation were captured, so no flows are recorded. Research ran in fixture mode with no live search: the only source behind kept findings (SRC-7a9ab6a3) describes itself as a test fixture and not real documentation, and both kept findings have low confidence. Four of the six findings were dropped at verification. Most research questions remain unanswered (see section 18, Limitations). Who may open the Team members screen at all is not decided and is not covered by any open question in this run.
- Open stale items: none
- Unresolved blocking issues: REQ-001 and REQ-002 carry the label Conflicting (mockup differs from decisions DEC-001 and DEC-003). Blocking open questions: Q-001, Q-002, Q-003, Q-006 (section 16).

## 2. Executive Summary

This feature lets team leads see the members of their own team and trigger a password reset for them, and lets every user change their own display name. The customer has decided what a lead sees (name, email, job title and account status, own team only), that a reset sends the member an emailed link while the lead never sees or sets the password, that every reset is logged with who did it and when, and that display names are 2 to 50 characters and need not be unique.

The mockup (one screen, "Team members") does not match those decisions in two places: it shows Name and Role rather than the agreed details, and it offers an enabled Reset password button on every row, including a Team lead row, which the customer ruled out. It also offers Change role and Delete user, for which no requirement exists. No screen shows where a display name is changed.

Key open decisions: how rows a lead may not reset are presented; whether Change role and Delete user belong to this feature; reset link lifetime, single use and effect on sessions; which account statuses may be reset; whether the Role column stays; and whether leads see the HR name or the display name. Research support is thin (one fixture source) and nothing in it settles these questions.

## 3. Goals and Scope

### Goals

- **FR-001** Team leads can view the members of their team. [Customer: REQ-001 · Conflicting] [Mockup: SCR-001]

## 8. Functional Requirements

### Team member list

Purpose: a team lead sees the members of their own team. User story: as a team lead, I see my team's members so that I can help them.

#### Confirmed requirements

- **FR-004** Team leads see the name, email, job title and account status of the members of their own team only, and no members of other teams. The mockup shows Name and Role only, which conflicts with this; whether Role stays visible is open (Q-007). [Customer: FEA-002 · Explicit] [Customer: REQ-001] [Decision: DEC-001] [Mockup: SCR-003]
- **FR-005** The team lead is the person recorded as the team's lead in HR; each team has one lead and each member belongs to one team. Visibility and reset rights depend on this HR data. [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]

#### Recommendations awaiting approval

None for this area.

#### Acceptance criteria

- **AC-001** Given a signed-in team lead whose team has members Ana and Ben and another team has member Carla, When the lead opens the member list, Then the list shows name, email, job title and account status for Ana and Ben only and does not show Carla. [Customer: FEA-002 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-001]

### Password reset

Purpose: a team lead triggers a password reset for a member of their own team.

#### Confirmed requirements

- **FR-006** A team lead may trigger a password reset only for members of their own team, and never for other team leads, administrators or themselves through this feature. The limit must hold for every reset request, not only in how the list is presented. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Customer: REQ-002] [Decision: DEC-003]
- **FR-007** A reset sends the member an email containing a link; the team lead never sees or sets the password. [Customer: FEA-005 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
- **FR-008** Every reset is logged with who did it and when. Where the log is kept and how it is accessed is not established. [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003] [Research: F-GAP-001-02]

#### Undecided behaviour

These lines record what must be decided. They are not requirements.

- **FR-009** Undecided: how rows the lead may not reset are presented (hidden, disabled with an explanation, or rejected on use) and whether the lead's own row is listed. The mockup shows an enabled Reset password button on the Team lead row. See Q-001. [Inferred: FEA-008 · Unknown] [Mockup: SCR-001]
- **FR-010** Undecided: how long a reset link stays valid, whether it is single use, and whether the member's current password and sessions stay valid until the link is used. See Q-003. [Inferred: FEA-009 · Unknown]
- **FR-011** Undecided: what the lead and member are told if the reset email cannot be delivered or the member has no usable email address. Whether delivery failure can be detected is not established. See Q-004. [Inferred: FEA-010 · Unknown]
- **FR-012** Undecided: which account statuses exist and whether a reset may be triggered for each. See Q-006. [Inferred: FEA-011 · Unknown]

#### Recommendations awaiting approval

- **FR-016** Recommendation, not a requirement: notify the member and require a new password at next sign-in after a reset by someone else. The only support is one fixture source with low confidence; the finding needs confirmation, and "forced change at next sign-in" suggests an operator-set password, which differs from the DEC-003 flow. See Q-005. [Research: FEA-006 · Research-supported] [Research: F-GAP-003-01]

#### Acceptance criteria

- **AC-002** Given team lead L and member M of L's team, When L triggers a password reset for M, Then M is sent an email containing a reset link and L is not shown or asked to set any password. [Customer: FEA-005 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
- **AC-003** Given team lead L, When L requests a reset for another team lead, an administrator, L themself, or a member of another team (by any route, not only the list), Then no reset is performed and no email is sent. How this is shown to L is undecided (FR-009). [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
- **AC-004** Given a reset has been performed for member M by lead L, When the reset completes, Then a log entry exists recording that L performed it and when. [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]

### Display name

Purpose: a user changes their own display name.

#### Confirmed requirements

- **FR-013** Users can change only their own display name, at any time; it must be 2 to 50 characters and need not be unique. Values outside the length limit are rejected with an error; the error wording is not established. No captured screen shows where it is changed. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Customer: REQ-003] [Decision: DEC-005]

#### Undecided behaviour

- **FR-014** Undecided: whether team leads see the HR name, the chosen display name, or both, and where a user changes their display name. Non-unique display names could make two members look identical in the reset list. See Q-008. [Inferred: FEA-013 · Unknown] [Assumption: ASM-G-002]

#### Recommendations awaiting approval

- **FR-017** Recommendation, not a requirement: consider whether display name changes should be recorded, since names are user-chosen and non-unique and a lead acts on members by name. The customer has not said whether they are audited. [Inferred: FEA-015 · Recommended (awaiting approval)]

#### Acceptance criteria

- **AC-005** Given a signed-in user U with display name "Sam", When U changes their display name to "Alex Kim" (8 characters), Then the new name is saved, and the save is not rejected even if another user already has that name. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-005]
- **AC-006** Given a signed-in user U, When U submits a display name of 1 character or of 51 characters, Then the change is rejected with an error and the old name is kept; names of exactly 2 and exactly 50 characters are accepted. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-005]
- **AC-007** Given signed-in users U and V, When U attempts to change V's display name, Then the change is not permitted. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-005]

## 17. Research Findings and Recommendations

Research ran in fixture mode with three fixture sources (SRC-7a9ab6a3, SRC-f3486c95, SRC-900a0021). Both kept findings rest on SRC-7a9ab6a3 alone, a self-declared test fixture and not independent authoritative evidence. Two findings were kept.

- F-GAP-001-02 (Research-supported, low confidence): the source says to limit who can reset passwords to roles authorised for it and to log each reset. It supports restricting resets to authorised operators and logging them (FR-006, FR-008). It does not say which roles are authorised (that comes from DEC-003), what to log, or how to present rows a lead cannot act on, so the hidden-versus-disabled question stays open (FR-009).
- F-GAP-003-01 (Research-supported, low confidence, needs confirmation): the source says that when someone resets another user's password, the account owner should be notified and required to choose a new password at next sign-in. It says nothing about link expiry, single use, sessions or delivery failure. It is presented only as a recommendation awaiting approval (FR-016), because it suggests an operator-set password, unlike the DEC-003 emailed-link flow.

1	# Team Member Management (Team Lead View): Feature Specification
2	
3	## 1. Document Status
4	
5	- Run ID: 20261013-033524-9f0985
6	- Date: 2026-10-13
7	- Run mode: fixture
8	- Publication status: pending final pass
9	- Known limitations: Capture is complete but covers one page in one static state (SCR-001); no links or navigation were captured, so no flows are recorded. Research ran in fixture mode with no live search: the only source behind kept findings (SRC-7a9ab6a3) describes itself as a test fixture and not real documentation, and both kept findings have low confidence. Four of the six findings were dropped at verification. Most research questions remain unanswered (see section 18, Limitations). Who may open the Team members screen at all is not decided and is not covered by any open question in this run.
10	- Open stale items: none
11	- Unresolved blocking issues: REQ-001 and REQ-002 carry the label Conflicting (mockup differs from decisions DEC-001 and DEC-003). Blocking open questions: Q-001, Q-002, Q-003, Q-006 (section 16).
12	
13	## 2. Executive Summary
14	
15	This feature lets team leads see the members of their own team and trigger a password reset for them, and lets every user change their own display name. The customer has decided what a lead sees (name, email, job title and account status, own team only), that a reset sends the member an emailed link while the lead never sees or sets the password, that every reset is logged with who did it and when, and that display names are 2 to 50 characters and need not be unique.
16	
17	The mockup (one screen, "Team members") does not match those decisions in two places: it shows Name and Role rather than the agreed details, and it offers an enabled Reset password button on every row, including a Team lead row, which the customer ruled out. It also offers Change role and Delete user, for which no requirement exists. No screen shows where a display name is changed.
18	
19	Key open decisions: how rows a lead may not reset are presented; whether Change role and Delete user belong to this feature; reset link lifetime, single use and effect on sessions; which account statuses may be reset; whether the Role column stays; and whether leads see the HR name or the display name. Research support is thin (one fixture source) and nothing in it settles these questions.
20	
21	## 3. Goals and Scope
22	
23	### Goals
24	
25	- **FR-001** Team leads can view the members of their team. [Customer: REQ-001 · Conflicting] [Mockup: SCR-001]
26	- **FR-002** Team leads can reset a team member's password, within the limits decided in DEC-003. [Customer: REQ-002 · Conflicting] [Decision: DEC-003]
27	- **FR-003** Users can change their own display name. [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-005]
28	
29	### In Scope
30	
31	The three goals above and the limits and behaviours the customer decided for them (DEC-001, DEC-002, DEC-003, DEC-005), as specified in section 8. Gaps approved at checkpoint 2 (DEC-006) that need a customer decision are listed in section 7 and section 16.
32	
33	### Out of Scope / Rejected
34	
35	No item was rejected by a decision, and the customer did not exclude any requirement in the supplied records. Exclusions are not inferred from the mockup. Change role and Delete user are shown in the mockup but their scope is undecided (FR-015), so they are neither in scope nor rejected.
36	
37	### Deferred
38	
39	Deferred at checkpoint 2 (Deferred: DEC-006). Nothing is specified for these in this document.
40	
41	- GAP-006: Reset audit log (Deferred: DEC-006)
42	- GAP-007: Effect of HR changes on team membership and lead rights (Deferred: DEC-006)
43	- GAP-009: Repeated or rapid reset requests (Deferred: DEC-006)
44	- GAP-010: Empty, loading, success and error states not shown (Deferred: DEC-006)
45	- GAP-011: Accessibility of repeated row actions and status feedback (Deferred: DEC-006)
46	- GAP-012: Display name validation details and messages (Deferred: DEC-006)
47	
48	## 4. Users and Roles
49	
50	- Team lead: the person recorded as the team's lead in HR; each team has one lead (DEC-002). May view own-team members and trigger resets for own-team members within the DEC-003 limits.
51	- Member: belongs to exactly one team (DEC-002). Can change their own display name (DEC-005).
52	- Administrator: named in DEC-003 as a role leads may not reset. How administrators are identified is not established; recorded as assumption ASM-F-001.
53	- Who may open the Team members screen, and who may use each action button, is not decided. The assumption that the captured screen is the team lead's view is ASM-G-001.
54	
55	## 5. Existing Mockup Coverage
56	
57	- SCR-001 (Observed): one screen, "Team members", a table of two rows (Ana Ruiz, Member; Ben Okafor, Team lead), each row with Reset password, Change role and Delete user buttons, all appearing enabled.
58	- SCR-002 (Observed): the table component; columns Name, Role and an unlabelled actions column. Identical button labels repeat on every row.
59	- SCR-003 (Observed): the team member entity shows two visible fields, Name and Role. Email, job title and account status are not shown.
60	- Flows: none captured.
61	- Ambiguous behaviour: who sees the screen and who can use each button; whether buttons differ by role (every row, including the Team lead row, shows all three); whether a user can act on their own row; which roles Change role offers; Delete user confirmation and permanence. These are carried into section 16 where a question exists.
62	- Capture limitations: one page, one static state, no navigation.
63	
64	## 6. Requirements Traceability
65	
66	| REQ | Requirement | Treatment | Label | References |
67	|---|---|---|---|---|
68	| REQ-001 | Team leads can view the members of their team. | partially addressed | Conflicting | FR-001, FR-004, FR-005, AC-001; DEC-001, DEC-002; mockup differs (SCR-003); Q-006, Q-007, Q-008, Q-009 |
69	| REQ-002 | Team leads can reset a team member's password. | partially addressed | Conflicting | FR-002, FR-006 to FR-012, AC-002 to AC-004; DEC-003, DEC-004; Q-001, Q-003, Q-004, Q-005, Q-006 |
70	| REQ-003 | Users can change their own display name. | partially addressed | Unknown | FR-003, FR-013, FR-014, AC-005 to AC-007; DEC-005; Q-008 |
71	
72	## 7. Gaps Identified
73	
74	| GAP | Gap | Approval | Path | Priority | Status | Rationale |
75	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
76	| GAP-001 | Reset password shown enabled on rows the lead may not reset | Approved: DEC-006 | both | critical | open (researched) | Mockup offers a forbidden action; presentation undecided; research did not answer it |
77	| GAP-002 | Change role and Delete user actions have no requirement | Approved: DEC-006 | customer | critical | open (customer decision pending) | Destructive and permission-changing actions with no requirement |
78	| GAP-003 | Reset link lifecycle, session handling and delivery failure undefined | Approved: DEC-006 | both | critical | open (researched) | Research covered notification only; expiry, single use, sessions, delivery failure unanswered |
79	| GAP-004 | Member details in the mockup differ from the agreed details | Approved: DEC-006 | customer | important | open (customer decision pending) | Name and Role shown; agreed list is name, email, job title, account status |
80	| GAP-005 | Changing one's own display name has no screen | Approved: DEC-006 | customer | important | open (customer decision pending) | No captured screen or flow; relation to the name leads see unknown |
81	| GAP-006 | Reset audit log: target, access and retention undecided | Deferred: DEC-006 | both | important | open (deferred by DEC-006) | Deferred at checkpoint 2 |
82	| GAP-007 | Effect of HR changes on team membership and lead rights | Deferred: DEC-006 | both | important | open (deferred by DEC-006) | Deferred at checkpoint 2 |
83	| GAP-008 | Account status values and their effect on resets | Approved: DEC-006 | customer | important | open (customer decision pending) | Statuses undefined; reset for inactive accounts undecided |
84	| GAP-009 | Repeated or rapid reset requests | Deferred: DEC-006 | research | important | open (deferred by DEC-006) | Deferred at checkpoint 2 |
85	| GAP-010 | Empty, loading, success and error states not shown | Deferred: DEC-006 | both | important | open (deferred by DEC-006) | Deferred at checkpoint 2 |
86	| GAP-011 | Accessibility of repeated row actions and status feedback | Deferred: DEC-006 | research | important | open (deferred by DEC-006) | Deferred at checkpoint 2 |
87	| GAP-012 | Display name validation details and messages | Deferred: DEC-006 | both | optional | open (deferred by DEC-006) | Deferred at checkpoint 2 |
88	| GAP-013 | List behaviour for large teams | Approved: DEC-006 | customer | optional | open (customer decision pending) | Team size and search, sort, paging not stated |
89	
90	## 8. Functional Requirements
91	
92	### Team member list
93	
94	Purpose: a team lead sees the members of their own team. User story: as a team lead, I see my team's members so that I can help them.
95	
96	#### Confirmed requirements
97	
98	- **FR-004** Team leads see the name, email, job title and account status of the members of their own team only, and no members of other teams. The mockup shows Name and Role only, which conflicts with this; whether Role stays visible is open (Q-007). [Customer: FEA-002 · Explicit] [Customer: REQ-001] [Decision: DEC-001] [Mockup: SCR-003]
99	- **FR-005** The team lead is the person recorded as the team's lead in HR; each team has one lead and each member belongs to one team. Visibility and reset rights depend on this HR data. [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
100	
101	#### Recommendations awaiting approval
102	
103	None for this area.
104	
105	#### Acceptance criteria
106	
107	- **AC-001** Given a signed-in team lead whose team has members Ana and Ben and another team has member Carla, When the lead opens the member list, Then the list shows name, email, job title and account status for Ana and Ben only and does not show Carla. [Customer: FEA-002 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-001]
108	
109	### Password reset
110	
111	Purpose: a team lead triggers a password reset for a member of their own team.
112	
113	#### Confirmed requirements
114	
115	- **FR-006** A team lead may trigger a password reset only for members of their own team, and never for other team leads, administrators or themselves through this feature. The limit must hold for every reset request, not only in how the list is presented. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Customer: REQ-002] [Decision: DEC-003]
116	- **FR-007** A reset sends the member an email containing a link; the team lead never sees or sets the password. [Customer: FEA-005 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
117	- **FR-008** Every reset is logged with who did it and when. Where the log is kept and how it is accessed is not established. [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003] [Research: F-GAP-001-02]
118	
119	#### Undecided behaviour
120	
121	These lines record what must be decided. They are not requirements.
122	
123	- **FR-009** Undecided: how rows the lead may not reset are presented (hidden, disabled with an explanation, or rejected on use) and whether the lead's own row is listed. The mockup shows an enabled Reset password button on the Team lead row. See Q-001. [Inferred: FEA-008 · Unknown] [Mockup: SCR-001]
124	- **FR-010** Undecided: how long a reset link stays valid, whether it is single use, and whether the member's current password and sessions stay valid until the link is used. See Q-003. [Inferred: FEA-009 · Unknown]
125	- **FR-011** Undecided: what the lead and member are told if the reset email cannot be delivered or the member has no usable email address. Whether delivery failure can be detected is not established. See Q-004. [Inferred: FEA-010 · Unknown]
126	- **FR-012** Undecided: which account statuses exist and whether a reset may be triggered for each. See Q-006. [Inferred: FEA-011 · Unknown]
127	
128	#### Recommendations awaiting approval
129	
130	- **FR-016** Recommendation, not a requirement: notify the member and require a new password at next sign-in after a reset by someone else. The only support is one fixture source with low confidence; the finding needs confirmation, and "forced change at next sign-in" suggests an operator-set password, which differs from the DEC-003 flow. See Q-005. [Research: FEA-006 · Research-supported] [Research: F-GAP-003-01]
131	
132	#### Acceptance criteria
133	
134	- **AC-002** Given team lead L and member M of L's team, When L triggers a password reset for M, Then M is sent an email containing a reset link and L is not shown or asked to set any password. [Customer: FEA-005 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
135	- **AC-003** Given team lead L, When L requests a reset for another team lead, an administrator, L themself, or a member of another team (by any route, not only the list), Then no reset is performed and no email is sent. How this is shown to L is undecided (FR-009). [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
136	- **AC-004** Given a reset has been performed for member M by lead L, When the reset completes, Then a log entry exists recording that L performed it and when. [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
137	
138	### Display name
139	
140	Purpose: a user changes their own display name.
141	
142	#### Confirmed requirements
143	
144	- **FR-013** Users can change only their own display name, at any time; it must be 2 to 50 characters and need not be unique. Values outside the length limit are rejected with an error; the error wording is not established. No captured screen shows where it is changed. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Customer: REQ-003] [Decision: DEC-005]
145	
146	#### Undecided behaviour
147	
148	- **FR-014** Undecided: whether team leads see the HR name, the chosen display name, or both, and where a user changes their display name. Non-unique display names could make two members look identical in the reset list. See Q-008. [Inferred: FEA-013 · Unknown] [Assumption: ASM-G-002]
149	
150	#### Recommendations awaiting approval
151	
152	- **FR-017** Recommendation, not a requirement: consider whether display name changes should be recorded, since names are user-chosen and non-unique and a lead acts on members by name. The customer has not said whether they are audited. [Inferred: FEA-015 · Recommended (awaiting approval)]
153	
154	#### Acceptance criteria
155	
156	- **AC-005** Given a signed-in user U with display name "Sam", When U changes their display name to "Alex Kim" (8 characters), Then the new name is saved, and the save is not rejected even if another user already has that name. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-005]
157	- **AC-006** Given a signed-in user U, When U submits a display name of 1 character or of 51 characters, Then the change is rejected with an error and the old name is kept; names of exactly 2 and exactly 50 characters are accepted. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-005]
158	- **AC-007** Given signed-in users U and V, When U attempts to change V's display name, Then the change is not permitted. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-005]
159	
160	### Other row actions shown in the mockup (Change role, Delete user)
161	
162	#### Undecided behaviour
163	
164	- **FR-015** Undecided: whether Change role and Delete user are part of this feature, who may use them, and for deletion the confirmation, permanence and effect on data and sessions. No requirement covers them, and changing roles in the app may conflict with HR being the source of who leads a team. See Q-002. [Inferred: FEA-012 · Unknown] [Mockup: SCR-002]
165	
166	No acceptance criteria are written for these actions until Q-002 is answered. Acceptance criteria for unauthorised viewers of the screen are not written because who may open it is undecided.
167	
168	## 9. State Transitions and Edge Cases
169	
170	### Password reset lifecycle
171	
172	| State | Event | Next state | Who can trigger | Provenance |
173	|---|---|---|---|---|
174	| No reset pending | Team lead triggers reset for an eligible own-team member (a log entry with who and when is recorded as part of this transition) | Reset email sent | Team lead of the member's team | [Customer: FEA-005 · Explicit] [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit] |
175	| Any | Lead requests reset for another lead, an administrator, themself or a member of another team | Unchanged; no reset performed | Not permitted for anyone through this feature | [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] |
176	| Reset email sent | Member uses the link | Unknown | Member | [Inferred: FEA-009 · Unknown] |
177	| Reset email sent | Link expires | Unknown | System | [Inferred: FEA-009 · Unknown] |
178	| Reset email sent | Email cannot be delivered | Unknown | System | [Inferred: FEA-010 · Unknown] |
179	
180	### Member account status lifecycle
181	
182	| State | Event | Next state | Who can trigger | Provenance |
183	|---|---|---|---|---|
184	| Unknown (statuses not defined) | Team lead triggers reset | Unknown | Team lead | [Inferred: FEA-011 · Unknown] |
185	
186	Edge cases not decided are recorded as open questions in section 16 or as undecided lines in section 8. Cases not shown in the capture are not specified here.
187	
188	## 10. Non-Functional Requirements
189	
190	No non-functional requirements are justified by the inputs or kept evidence. No performance, availability or compliance figures were supplied, and none are invented.
191	
192	- **NFR-001** Undecided: typical and maximum team size, and whether the member list needs search, sort or paging. No team size figures are available. See Q-009. [Inferred: FEA-014 · Unknown]
193	
194	## 11. Data Model and Business Rules
195	
196	No schema was inspected. Entities and fields below come from the mockup and decisions only.
197	
198	- Team member (user): Name and Role are visible in the mockup (SCR-003, Observed). Email, job title and account status are named by DEC-001 but not shown in the capture. Display name is named by DEC-005; its relation to Name is undecided (FR-014).
199	- Team: one lead and its members; derived from HR records (DEC-002). How HR data reaches this feature is not established (ASM-F-002).
200	- Reset log entry: who and when (DEC-003); further content is not decided.
201	
202	- **BR-001** The team lead is the person recorded as the team's lead in HR; each team has one lead and each member belongs to one team. [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
203	- **BR-002** A display name is 2 to 50 characters and need not be unique. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-005]
204	- **BR-003** A team lead never sees or sets a member's password; the member receives a reset link by email. [Customer: FEA-005 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
205	
206	## 12. Screens and User Flows
207	
208	- SCR-001 Team members (Observed): the only captured screen; see section 5.
209	- Flows: none captured. The buttons have no visible destination. No screen exists for changing a display name (FR-014).
210	
211	## 13. Integrations and Dependencies
212	
213	- HR records: define team membership and leadership (FEA-003, Explicit). How the feature obtains this data is not established; the assumption that it is available is ASM-F-002.
214	- Email: a reset sends a link by email (FEA-005, Explicit). How email is sent today and whether delivery failures can be detected are not established.
215	- Administrator status: needed to enforce the DEC-003 exclusion; where it is recorded is not established (ASM-F-001).
216	
217	## 14. Security, Privacy, and Error Handling
218	
219	- Reset limits and the "never sees or sets the password" rule are in FR-006, FR-007 and BR-003; logging is in FR-008.
220	- Visibility is limited to the lead's own team (FR-004).
221	- Undecided and unspecified: link lifetime and sessions (FR-010), delivery failure (FR-011), presentation of ineligible rows (FR-009), account status (FR-012), Delete user and Change role (FR-015).
222	- Error handling for invalid display names: values outside 2 to 50 characters are rejected with an error (FR-013); wording is not established.
223

1	# Team Member Management (Team Lead View): Feature Specification
2	
3	## 1. Document Status
4	
5	- Run ID: 20261013-033524-9f0985
6	- Date: 2026-10-13
7	- Run mode: fixture
8	- Publication status: pending final pass
9	- Known limitations: Capture is complete but covers one page in one static state (SCR-001); no links or navigation were captured, so no flows are recorded. Research ran in fixture mode with no live search: the only source behind kept findings (SRC-7a9ab6a3) describes itself as a test fixture and not real documentation, and both kept findings have low confidence. Four of the six findings were dropped at verification. Most research questions remain unanswered (see section 18, Limitations). Who may open the Team members screen at all is not decided and is not covered by any open question in this run.
10	- Open stale items: none
11	- Unresolved blocking issues: REQ-001 and REQ-002 carry the label Conflicting (mockup differs from decisions DEC-001 and DEC-003). Blocking open questions: Q-001, Q-002, Q-003, Q-006 (section 16).
12	
13	## 2. Executive Summary
14	
15	This feature lets team leads see the members of their own team and trigger a password reset for them, and lets every user change their own display name. The customer has decided what a lead sees (name, email, job title and account status, own team only), that a reset sends the member an emailed link while the lead never sees or sets the password, that every reset is logged with who did it and when, and that display names are 2 to 50 characters and need not be unique.
16	
17	The mockup (one screen, "Team members") does not match those decisions in two places: it shows Name and Role rather than the agreed details, and it offers an enabled Reset password button on every row, including a Team lead row, which the customer ruled out. It also offers Change role and Delete user, for which no requirement exists. No screen shows where a display name is changed.
18	
19	Key open decisions: how rows a lead may not reset are presented; whether Change role and Delete user belong to this feature; reset link lifetime, single use and effect on sessions; which account statuses may be reset; whether the Role column stays; and whether leads see the HR name or the display name. Research support is thin (one fixture source) and nothing in it settles these questions.
20	
21	## 3. Goals and Scope
22	
23	### Goals
24	
25	- **FR-001** Team leads can view the members of their team. [Customer: REQ-001 · Conflicting] [Mockup: SCR-001]
26	- **FR-002** Team leads can reset a team member's password, within the limits decided in DEC-003. [Customer: REQ-002 · Conflicting] [Decision: DEC-003]
27	- **FR-003** Users can change their own display name. [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-005]
28	
29	### In Scope
30	
31	The three goals above and the limits and behaviours the customer decided for them (DEC-001, DEC-002, DEC-003, DEC-005), as specified in section 8. Gaps approved at checkpoint 2 (DEC-006) that need a customer decision are listed in section 7 and section 16.
32	
33	### Out of Scope / Rejected
34	
35	No item was rejected by a decision, and the customer did not exclude any requirement in the supplied records. Exclusions are not inferred from the mockup. Change role and Delete user are shown in the mockup but their scope is undecided (FR-015), so they are neither in scope nor rejected.
36	
37	### Deferred
38	
39	Deferred at checkpoint 2 (Deferred: DEC-006). Nothing is specified for these in this document.
40	
41	- GAP-006: Reset audit log (Deferred: DEC-006)
42	- GAP-007: Effect of HR changes on team membership and lead rights (Deferred: DEC-006)
43	- GAP-009: Repeated or rapid reset requests (Deferred: DEC-006)
44	- GAP-010: Empty, loading, success and error states not shown (Deferred: DEC-006)
45	- GAP-011: Accessibility of repeated row actions and status feedback (Deferred: DEC-006)
46	- GAP-012: Display name validation details and messages (Deferred: DEC-006)
47	
48	## 4. Users and Roles
49	
50	- Team lead: the person recorded as the team's lead in HR; each team has one lead (DEC-002). May view own-team members and trigger resets for own-team members within the DEC-003 limits.
51	- Member: belongs to exactly one team (DEC-002). Can change their own display name (DEC-005).
52	- Administrator: named in DEC-003 as a role leads may not reset. How administrators are identified is not established; recorded as assumption ASM-F-001.
53	- Who may open the Team members screen, and who may use each action button, is not decided. The assumption that the captured screen is the team lead's view is ASM-G-001.
54	
55	## 5. Existing Mockup Coverage
56	
57	- SCR-001 (Observed): one screen, "Team members", a table of two rows (Ana Ruiz, Member; Ben Okafor, Team lead), each row with Reset password, Change role and Delete user buttons, all appearing enabled.
58	- SCR-002 (Observed): the table component; columns Name, Role and an unlabelled actions column. Identical button labels repeat on every row.
59	- SCR-003 (Observed): the team member entity shows two visible fields, Name and Role. Email, job title and account status are not shown.
60	- Flows: none captured.
61	- Ambiguous behaviour: who sees the screen and who can use each button; whether buttons differ by role (every row, including the Team lead row, shows all three); whether a user can act on their own row; which roles Change role offers; Delete user confirmation and permanence. These are carried into section 16 where a question exists.
62	- Capture limitations: one page, one static state, no navigation.
63	
64	## 6. Requirements Traceability
65	
66	| REQ | Requirement | Treatment | Label | References |
67	|---|---|---|---|---|
68	| REQ-001 | Team leads can view the members of their team. | partially addressed | Conflicting | FR-001, FR-004, FR-005, AC-001; DEC-001, DEC-002; mockup differs (SCR-003); Q-006, Q-007, Q-008, Q-009 |
69	| REQ-002 | Team leads can reset a team member's password. | partially addressed | Conflicting | FR-002, FR-006 to FR-012, AC-002 to AC-004; DEC-003, DEC-004; Q-001, Q-003, Q-004, Q-005, Q-006 |
70	| REQ-003 | Users can change their own display name. | partially addressed | Unknown | FR-003, FR-013, FR-014, AC-005 to AC-007; DEC-005; Q-008 |
71	
72	## 7. Gaps Identified
73	
74	| GAP | Gap | Approval | Path | Priority | Status | Rationale |
75	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
76	| GAP-001 | Reset password shown enabled on rows the lead may not reset | Approved: DEC-006 | both | critical | open (researched) | Mockup offers a forbidden action; presentation undecided; research did not answer it |
77	| GAP-002 | Change role and Delete user actions have no requirement | Approved: DEC-006 | customer | critical | open (customer decision pending) | Destructive and permission-changing actions with no requirement |
78	| GAP-003 | Reset link lifecycle, session handling and delivery failure undefined | Approved: DEC-006 | both | critical | open (researched) | Research covered notification only; expiry, single use, sessions, delivery failure unanswered |
79	| GAP-004 | Member details in the mockup differ from the agreed details | Approved: DEC-006 | customer | important | open (customer decision pending) | Name and Role shown; agreed list is name, email, job title, account status |
80	| GAP-005 | Changing one's own display name has no screen | Approved: DEC-006 | customer | important | open (customer decision pending) | No captured screen or flow; relation to the name leads see unknown |
81	| GAP-006 | Reset audit log: target, access and retention undecided | Deferred: DEC-006 | both | important | open (deferred by DEC-006) | Deferred at checkpoint 2 |
82	| GAP-007 | Effect of HR changes on team membership and lead rights | Deferred: DEC-006 | both | important | open (deferred by DEC-006) | Deferred at checkpoint 2 |
83	| GAP-008 | Account status values and their effect on resets | Approved: DEC-006 | customer | important | open (customer decision pending) | Statuses undefined; reset for inactive accounts undecided |
84	| GAP-009 | Repeated or rapid reset requests | Deferred: DEC-006 | research | important | open (deferred by DEC-006) | Deferred at checkpoint 2 |
85	| GAP-010 | Empty, loading, success and error states not shown | Deferred: DEC-006 | both | important | open (deferred by DEC-006) | Deferred at checkpoint 2 |
86	| GAP-011 | Accessibility of repeated row actions and status feedback | Deferred: DEC-006 | research | important | open (deferred by DEC-006) | Deferred at checkpoint 2 |
87	| GAP-012 | Display name validation details and messages | Deferred: DEC-006 | both | optional | open (deferred by DEC-006) | Deferred at checkpoint 2 |
88	| GAP-013 | List behaviour for large teams | Approved: DEC-006 | customer | optional | open (customer decision pending) | Team size and search, sort, paging not stated |
89	
90	## 8. Functional Requirements
91	
92	### Team member list
93	
94	Purpose: a team lead sees the members of their own team. User story: as a team lead, I see my team's members so that I can help them.
95	
96	#### Confirmed requirements
97	
98	- **FR-004** Team leads see the name, email, job title and account status of the members of their own team only, and no members of other teams. The mockup shows Name and Role only, which conflicts with this; whether Role stays visible is open (Q-007). [Customer: FEA-002 · Explicit] [Customer: REQ-001] [Decision: DEC-001] [Mockup: SCR-003]
99	- **FR-005** The team lead is the person recorded as the team's lead in HR; each team has one lead and each member belongs to one team. Visibility and reset rights depend on this HR data. [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
100	
101	#### Recommendations awaiting approval
102	
103	None for this area.
104	
105	#### Acceptance criteria
106	
107	- **AC-001** Given a signed-in team lead whose team has members Ana and Ben and another team has member Carla, When the lead opens the member list, Then the list shows name, email, job title and account status for Ana and Ben only and does not show Carla. [Customer: FEA-002 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-001]
108	
109	### Password reset
110	
111	Purpose: a team lead triggers a password reset for a member of their own team.
112	
113	#### Confirmed requirements
114	
115	- **FR-006** A team lead may trigger a password reset only for members of their own team, and never for other team leads, administrators or themselves through this feature. The limit must hold for every reset request, not only in how the list is presented. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Customer: REQ-002] [Decision: DEC-003]
116	- **FR-007** A reset sends the member an email containing a link; the team lead never sees or sets the password. [Customer: FEA-005 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
117	- **FR-008** Every reset is logged with who did it and when. Where the log is kept and how it is accessed is not established. [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003] [Research: F-GAP-001-02]
118	
119	#### Undecided behaviour
120	
121	These lines record what must be decided. They are not requirements.
122	
123	- **FR-009** Undecided: how rows the lead may not reset are presented (hidden, disabled with an explanation, or rejected on use) and whether the lead's own row is listed. The mockup shows an enabled Reset password button on the Team lead row. See Q-001. [Inferred: FEA-008 · Unknown] [Mockup: SCR-001]
124	- **FR-010** Undecided: how long a reset link stays valid, whether it is single use, and whether the member's current password and sessions stay valid until the link is used. See Q-003. [Inferred: FEA-009 · Unknown]
125	- **FR-011** Undecided: what the lead and member are told if the reset email cannot be delivered or the member has no usable email address. Whether delivery failure can be detected is not established. See Q-004. [Inferred: FEA-010 · Unknown]
126	- **FR-012** Undecided: which account statuses exist and whether a reset may be triggered for each. See Q-006. [Inferred: FEA-011 · Unknown]
127	
128	#### Recommendations awaiting approval
129	
130	- **FR-016** Recommendation, not a requirement: notify the member and require a new password at next sign-in after a reset by someone else. The only support is one fixture source with low confidence; the finding needs confirmation, and "forced change at next sign-in" suggests an operator-set password, which differs from the DEC-003 flow. See Q-005. [Research: FEA-006 · Research-supported] [Research: F-GAP-003-01]
131	
132	#### Acceptance criteria
133	
134	- **AC-002** Given team lead L and member M of L's team, When L triggers a password reset for M, Then M is sent an email containing a reset link and L is not shown or asked to set any password. [Customer: FEA-005 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
135	- **AC-003** Given team lead L, When L requests a reset for another team lead, an administrator, L themself, or a member of another team (by any route, not only the list), Then no reset is performed and no email is sent. How this is shown to L is undecided (FR-009). [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
136	- **AC-004** Given a reset has been performed for member M by lead L, When the reset completes, Then a log entry exists recording that L performed it and when. [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
137	
138	### Display name
139	
140	Purpose: a user changes their own display name.
141	
142	#### Confirmed requirements
143	
144	- **FR-013** Users can change only their own display name, at any time; it must be 2 to 50 characters and need not be unique. Values outside the length limit are rejected with an error; the error wording is not established. No captured screen shows where it is changed. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Customer: REQ-003] [Decision: DEC-005]
145	
146	#### Undecided behaviour
147	
148	- **FR-014** Undecided: whether team leads see the HR name, the chosen display name, or both, and where a user changes their display name. Non-unique display names could make two members look identical in the reset list. See Q-008. [Inferred: FEA-013 · Unknown] [Assumption: ASM-G-002]
149	
150	#### Recommendations awaiting approval
151	
152	- **FR-017** Recommendation, not a requirement: consider whether display name changes should be recorded, since names are user-chosen and non-unique and a lead acts on members by name. The customer has not said whether they are audited. [Inferred: FEA-015 · Recommended (awaiting approval)]
153	
154	#### Acceptance criteria
155	
156	- **AC-005** Given a signed-in user U with display name "Sam", When U changes their display name to "Alex Kim" (8 characters), Then the new name is saved, and the save is not rejected even if another user already has that name. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-005]
157	- **AC-006** Given a signed-in user U, When U submits a display name of 1 character or of 51 characters, Then the change is rejected with an error and the old name is kept; names of exactly 2 and exactly 50 characters are accepted. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-005]
158	- **AC-007** Given signed-in users U and V, When U attempts to change V's display name, Then the change is not permitted. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-005]
159	
160	### Other row actions shown in the mockup (Change role, Delete user)
161	
162	#### Undecided behaviour
163	
164	- **FR-015** Undecided: whether Change role and Delete user are part of this feature, who may use them, and for deletion the confirmation, permanence and effect on data and sessions. No requirement covers them, and changing roles in the app may conflict with HR being the source of who leads a team. See Q-002. [Inferred: FEA-012 · Unknown] [Mockup: SCR-002]
165	
166	No acceptance criteria are written for these actions until Q-002 is answered. Acceptance criteria for unauthorised viewers of the screen are not written because who may open it is undecided.
167	
168	## 9. State Transitions and Edge Cases
169	
170	### Password reset lifecycle
171	
172	| State | Event | Next state | Who can trigger | Provenance |
173	|---|---|---|---|---|
174	| No reset pending | Team lead triggers reset for an eligible own-team member (a log entry with who and when is recorded as part of this transition) | Reset email sent | Team lead of the member's team | [Customer: FEA-005 · Explicit] [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit] |
175	| Any | Lead requests reset for another lead, an administrator, themself or a member of another team | Unchanged; no reset performed | Not permitted for anyone through this feature | [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] |
176	| Reset email sent | Member uses the link | Unknown | Member | [Inferred: FEA-009 · Unknown] |
177	| Reset email sent | Link expires | Unknown | System | [Inferred: FEA-009 · Unknown] |
178	| Reset email sent | Email cannot be delivered | Unknown | System | [Inferred: FEA-010 · Unknown] |
179	
180	### Member account status lifecycle
181	
182	| State | Event | Next state | Who can trigger | Provenance |
183	|---|---|---|---|---|
184	| Unknown (statuses not defined) | Team lead triggers reset | Unknown | Team lead | [Inferred: FEA-011 · Unknown] |
185	
186	Edge cases not decided are recorded as open questions in section 16 or as undecided lines in section 8. Cases not shown in the capture are not specified here.
187
